Subject: Acuity committed numbers — initial ask on HW timing & vendor options

Hey team,

Acuity is taking us to a committed reserved-capacity decision point in the next 6–9 weeks. High-level ask from the AE/procurement side: they want to lock a Dedicated pool that effectively maps to ~100 H100-equivalent instances (we've been modelling as 120 nodes to cover headroom) across two delivery tranches tied to their product ramp (Q2 and Q3 2028).

Key asks for infra/procurement coordination:
- Can we get OEM lead-time windows for a matching SKU (H100-class) with quantity splits (50/70) and potential earlier partial shipments?
- Need a cloud backstop plan (region: us-west) for ~20% of committed throughput if hardware slips — Orion Cloud introduced as a likely channel.
- Any recommendations on batching shipments to reduce freight/customs overheads while preserving onboarding cadence?

I attached the rough ACME (Acuity) proposal and our estimate sheet. Procurement will request a mutual action plan once we have vendor ETAs and a fallback cloud commitment.

Thanks — this is high priority for the deal team.

Ben

Priyom / Ben —

Thanks for the heads-up. Quick initial reactions from infra/procurement POV:

1) Split strategy: rather than 50/70, I'd prefer a three-tranche approach: 40 (Q2), 40 (early Q3), 40 (late Q3). That gives us more flexibility to absorb one delayed tranche without breaching SLAs.
2) OEM lead times: QuantumParts (our usual OEM channel) is quoting 16–20 weeks for bulk H100-class backfills right now; lead time varies a bit by thermal config and power cabs. I can ask for a firm commitment window and block slots if we provide a deposit.
3) Cloud backstop: Orion's offering to reserve a pool for a 6–9 month term is reasonable cost-wise; we should cap backstop to 20–25% and use it only for early-onboarding traffic.
4) SKU batching: group by rack/PDUs and ship in 20–40 node blocks to simplify racking. Shipping in smaller batches increases install ops overhead; larger batches increase customs/risk.

I attached a first-pass SKU mapping to align SKUs -> on-prem config.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Dedicated Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachments: SKU_mapping_v1.csv (csv)
